convoLines.text: "What's the kindest thing someone's done for you out here? That's the whole of it."
"That's the good stuff. Quiet generosity. It's holding this whole thing together."
"Saw things with too many joints. Give them room. That's the whole lesson."
"Someone saved me the last of the stew once. Didn't say anything, just put the bowl down and walked off. I think about that bowl more than I think about the monsters."
"...What's that supposed to mean?" Their voice goes careful.
"What's this about? Still on the kindest thing someone's done for you."
"All right. Thank you for asking."
"Not right now. I've got my own things to handle."
"Anyway — I should get back to it. Good talking, though."
They fill the quiet. "Anyway — where was I?"
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"What's something from your old life that's actually useful here?"
"Not dumb at all. The people who can't wait are the ones who make mistakes. You're an asset."
"Being a tattoo artist taught me to read people fast — who's lying, who's scared, who needs a job. Turns out that's a survival skill. Who knew."
"Still on your useful old-life skills."
"Someone should watch your back. Might as well be me."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"Good question." "Moshe always took the burnt piece. Said someone had to. I take it now."
"I braid grass while listening to plans. It doesn't bring anyone back. It just keeps my hands from shaking."
"Nobody says Moshe's name right yet. We will. Give it a few days."
You show them Cattail — where it grows, how to tell it apart. A short laugh. "And I've been walking past it for weeks."
"Right. Go on, then."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Hm. Never mind — go on."
"You told me about people sharing food they couldn't spare. Quiet. No performance. Seen it again since?"
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Sure — what's on your mind?"
Something crosses their face — quick, then gone. The practiced expression clicks back into place.
"I don't actually want to belong somewhere. I want to prove they're useful. It's safer if people don't know. Please don't tell the others."
Aria looks at you, level. "I told you the truth. You can keep poking it, but it's told."
"So." They look at the fire for a moment.
"Still on that personal stuff."
They hear the warmth in it. They're not ready to let it in.
"...Fine. This had better be worth it."
You show them Wild Ginger — where it grows, how to tell it apart. "Huh." They turn it over in their mind. "I'll remember that one."
"Alright, duty calls. This was a good pause."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"This was good." They mean it.
"About that question — Did you sleep? I kept hearing things out past the treeline."
They go still. "So it's not just me. Good. That's... good to know. Bad, but good."
The ease drains out of it, a little.
"Still on how you slept."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"Huh. Let me think about that." "Huh. I answered that once — back when the answer was simpler." "Moshe owed me a favor. I keep thinking about collecting. Stupid."
"That's... pretty much all of it, honestly."
They glance at the fire, then back. The quiet doesn't seem to bother them.
"Anyway." A small smile.
"Sure. I'll be around."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Have you heard anything? About the taken. The pods. Anything at all."
"I see." They take a moment to think about your answer.
Something in them almost softens — then doesn't. Not yet.

"It's my mother, Karen. Was taken at the Scattering. The boring half. She made soup from nothing and they called that boring. Some nights I swear I hear them before I sleep -- the pods, rows deep, humming.
Then morning comes and I can't say whether it was real.
"Forget I said anything. What did you want? That's where we are."
"Saw things with too many joints. Give them room. That's the whole lesson."
"Good question." "They took Sang-hyun — Siege, on the screens. The whole fire watched. Nobody knew where to look."
"Same weather, different day. I keep notes."
"Still on what's been happening."
"Oh — okay. Later, then."
"Thanks for listening. Most people change the subject."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"About that question — What scares you most about what's happening? The real answer."
They go quiet. "Yeah. Me too. The randomness would almost be kinder."
Their friendliness thins — still there, just held at arm's length.
"Still on what scares you most."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want? Does that make sense?"
"Huh. Let me think about that." "You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "Siege. They just... took Sang-hyun. Came back like nothing happened. It wasn't nothing."
They nod slowly, not quite done, not quite continuing.
They fill the quiet. "Anyway — where was I?"
"Oh — okay. Later, then."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"Can I tell you something? At night I talk to someone who isn't there anymore."
"This one — Rosary Pea. Leaf, stem, smell. You won't forget it now."
"Anyway." A small smile.
"Still on their secret."
They hear the warmth in it. They're not ready to let it in.
"Don't tell anyone I told you. What's on your mind?"
"Huh. Let me think about that." I'm not trying to be a hero. I'm trying to be necessary.
"Watch. Just — watch. I'll show every doubter what I'm made of."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Sure. I'll be around."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"I'm not sure, but Can I tell you something? I'm practicing what I would say if I ever saw my family again. I haven't told anyone."
"Come get air with me. I need to think out loud."
"Here. I made an extra." Donna presses something into your hand — a decent tool, oiled and kept. (Useful. Keep it.)
"Still on their secret."
"...Hi. Sorry. I'm not good at the talking-to-strangers part."
Something eases in their shoulders. "Oh. Okay. That's... that's fine, then."
You show them Rosary Pea — where it grows, how to tell it apart. They nod slowly, committing it to memory. "Good to know. Really good to know."
"...Anyway. What did you want to ask? …sorry."
"You want to know about that? Okay." "I'd follow you out past the treeline. Don't tell the others — they'd want to come too."
"People here talk. What they say about you when you're not at the fire — that's the real answer to your question."
"Well." A breath. "That's where things stand."
"I should go. You know where to find me."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
